meetings.name: VTA (Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority) Board of Directors
meetings.decides: VTA (Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority) runs buses, light rail and county transit projects. Its Board of Directors, made up of local elected officials, sets VTA policy and votes on budgets and projects.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the first Thursday of the month at 5:30 pm
usualSchedule.note: Some months may be skipped, so check the calendar before you go.

meetings.place: Board of Supervisors' Chambers, County Government Center, 70 West Hedding Street, San José
meetings.watchOnline: You can join by Zoom or phone, or watch on VTA's YouTube channel. The links are on each meeting's agenda page.
howToComment: Email your comment to board.secretary@vta.org. VTA encourages written comments by noon on the meeting day, and it shares them with the Board.
To speak in person, fill out a speaker card at the information table before the item is heard.
To speak online, join the Zoom link from the agenda page. When the chair calls the item, click raise hand, or press *9 on a phone.
Plan for one minute to speak. Check the agenda page for the exact rules that day.

meetings.name: Metropolitan Transportation Commission (MTC)
meetings.decides: MTC (Metropolitan Transportation Commission) is the regional planning and funding agency for the nine Bay Area counties. Its Commission decides how regional money is shared with transit and sets regional transportation plans.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the fourth Wednesday of the month
usualSchedule.note: Some months move, so check the calendar before you go.

meetings.place: Bay Area Metro Center, 375 Beale Street, San Francisco. The 1st floor room is listed on each agenda.
meetings.watchOnline: You can watch the live webcast or join by Zoom or phone. Open the meeting on the MTC calendar to find the links.
howToComment: Email info@bayareametro.gov by 5 pm two business days before the meeting. Put the meeting name and agenda item number in the subject line.
To speak online, join the Zoom link from the meeting page. When the chair calls your item, use raise hand.
To speak by phone, call the Zoom number, enter the webinar ID, and press *9 to raise your hand. Press *6 to unmute when called.
To speak in person, go to 375 Beale Street. Ask the Clerk for a request to speak card, fill it out and hand it back.

meetings.name: Caltrain Board (Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board)
meetings.decides: Caltrain is the regional train line between San Francisco, San José and Gilroy. It is run by the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board, shared by San Francisco, San Mateo and Santa Clara counties, which votes on the budget, fares, service and major projects.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the first Thursday of the month at 9 am, with no meeting in July

meetings.place: Public Hearing Room, 5th Floor, 166 North Rollins Road, Millbrae
meetings.watchOnline: You can join by Zoom, and past meeting videos are posted on the Caltrain website. Zoom links are on each meeting page.
howToComment: Email publiccomment@caltrain.com. Sending it by 2 pm the day before is safest. The agenda lists the latest time it can still reach the Board.
Speakers usually get one minute, or two minutes on items the Board votes on. The agenda gives the limits for that day.
To speak live, come to the Millbrae meeting room or join the Zoom link on the agenda. On Zoom, click Raise Hand. By phone, press *9, then *6 to unmute.
Names and email addresses in comments become public records.

meetings.name: BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) Board of Directors
meetings.decides: BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) runs the train system linking the East Bay, San Francisco, the Peninsula and the South Bay. Its nine elected directors approve the budget, fares, service levels and big projects.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the second and fourth Thursdays of the month, except November and December
usualSchedule.note: In November and December the dates change, so check the calendar. Meetings usually start at 9 am, but times can vary.

meetings.place: BART Board Room, 2150 Webster Street, Oakland
meetings.watchOnline: You can watch live or past meetings at bart.gov/boardtv, or join by Zoom or phone. The Zoom link and call-in number are on each agenda.
howToComment: Email your comment before the meeting with "public comment" as the subject. Each agenda gives the address and deadline, recently Board.Meeting@BART.gov by 3 pm two days before.
You can also use the comment form on the Contact the BART Board page.
To speak in person, fill out a Request to Speak form at the Board Room door. On Zoom, click Raise Hand, or press *9 by phone. Each speaker gets two minutes.
Check the agenda for the Zoom link, phone number and any changes to these rules.

meetings.name: SamTrans (San Mateo County Transit District) Board of Directors
meetings.decides: SamTrans (San Mateo County Transit District) runs buses in San Mateo County and is one of the agencies behind Caltrain. Its Board votes on bus service, fares, the budget and projects.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the first Wednesday of the month at 2 pm

meetings.place: Public Hearing Room, 5th Floor, 166 North Rollins Road, Millbrae
meetings.watchOnline: You can come in person or join by Zoom. The Zoom details are on each agenda, and past videos are on the SamTrans website.
howToComment: Email publiccomment@samtrans.com. Sending it by 2 pm the day before is safest. The agenda lists the latest time it can still reach the Board.
Each speaker usually gets one minute. The agenda gives the exact rules for that day.
To speak live, come to the Millbrae meeting room or join the Zoom link on the agenda. On Zoom, click Raise Hand. By phone, press *9, then *6 to unmute.
Names and email addresses in comments become public records.

meetings.name: SFMTA (San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency) Board of Directors
meetings.decides: SFMTA (San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency) runs Muni buses, trains and cable cars, plus city streets, parking and taxis. Its seven member Board, appointed by the mayor, approves the budget, sets policy and picks the agency's director.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the first and third Tuesday of the month at 1 pm
usualSchedule.note: The Board sometimes moves a meeting, so check the calendar before you go.

meetings.place: City Hall, Room 400, 1 Dr. Carlton B. Goodlett Place, San Francisco
meetings.watchOnline: You can watch live on SFGovTV2 (San Francisco's government TV channel), on cable channel 78, or online at sfgovtv.org/sfmtaLIVE.
howToComment: To speak in person, go to City Hall, Room 400. The agency says public comment is taken on each item before or during the Board's talk about it. Ask staff there how to sign up.
To write instead, email MTABoard@sfmta.com. The Board asks for comments by noon the day before the meeting so members can read them in advance.
Online or phone comment is only offered on request, for people with a disability who cannot come in person. Ask the Board Secretary at 415-646-4470 at least three hours before the meeting.

meetings.name: AC Transit (Alameda-Contra Costa Transit District) Board of Directors
meetings.decides: AC Transit (Alameda-Contra Costa Transit District) runs buses in Alameda and Contra Costa counties and across the bridges to San Francisco and the Peninsula. Its seven elected directors set bus service, fares and the budget.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the second and fourth Wednesday of the month at 5 pm, with only one meeting in August, November and December

meetings.place: 1600 Franklin Street, 2nd Floor Board Room, Oakland
meetings.watchOnline: You can join by Zoom or by phone. The link and phone number are on each meeting's agenda and on the public meetings calendar.
howToComment: To speak in person, fill out a speaker card when you arrive and give it to the District Secretary. Walk to the lectern when your name is called. You get two minutes.
To speak online, join the Zoom link from the agenda and click Raise Hand. By phone, press *9 to raise your hand and *6 to unmute when called. You get two minutes.
To write instead, use the online comment form. Comments sent before 3 pm on the meeting day are more likely to be read by the Board before the meeting starts.

meetings.name: SMART Board of Directors (Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit)
meetings.decides: SMART (Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit) runs passenger trains and a bike and walking path in Sonoma and Marin counties. Its 12 member Board, mostly local elected officials, approves the budget, contracts and train service.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the third Wednesday of the month at 1:30 pm
usualSchedule.note: The Board cancels a meeting when it is not needed, so check the calendar before you go.

meetings.watchOnline: You can watch the livestream on SMART's website, or join by Zoom or phone. The links and phone numbers are on SMART's Watch a Board Meeting page.
howToComment: To comment in writing, email Board@SonomaMarinTrain.org. SMART strongly encourages this and asks for it by 5 pm the day before the meeting.
To speak in person, go to the Petaluma office and speak when the Chair opens public comment. Speakers are asked to keep to two minutes.
To speak online, join the Zoom webinar from the agenda link, or phone in using the number on the agenda. Verbal comment by Zoom or phone can be limited by technology, so emailing is safest.

meetings.name: WETA (Water Emergency Transportation Authority) Board, which runs San Francisco Bay Ferry
meetings.decides: WETA (Water Emergency Transportation Authority) runs San Francisco Bay Ferry. Its five member Board approves ferry routes, schedules, fares, the budget and contracts for boats and terminals.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the second Thursday of the month at 1 pm. Some months are cancelled.
usualSchedule.note: Dates, times and places can change, so check the calendar before you go.

meetings.watchOnline: You can join by Zoom or by phone. The link and phone numbers are on each meeting's agenda.
howToComment: To speak in person, go to the meeting place listed on that month's agenda, which changes. Fill out a speaker card. You get up to three minutes.
To speak online or by phone, join the Zoom meeting listed on the agenda and wait to be called. You also get up to three minutes.
To sign up ahead of time, email BoardOfDirectors@sfbayferry.com with your name and the agenda item number. Send it no later than 15 minutes after the meeting starts. Comments are also taken live.

meetings.name: Golden Gate Bridge, Highway and Transportation District Board of Directors
meetings.decides: The Golden Gate Bridge, Highway and Transportation District runs the bridge, Golden Gate Transit buses and Golden Gate Ferry. Its 19 member Board of elected officials and appointed public members sets tolls, fares, service and the budget.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the fourth Friday of the month at 10 am
usualSchedule.note: Meetings near the holidays sometimes move to the third Friday, and the Board may meet in one of the other counties it serves, so check the calendar.

meetings.place: Board Room, Administration Building, Golden Gate Bridge Toll Plaza, San Francisco
meetings.watchOnline: You can join by Zoom or by phone. The phone number and webinar ID are on each meeting's agenda.
howToComment: To speak in person, go to the meeting. People in the room are called first, then people online or on the phone. You get up to three minutes.
To speak by Zoom, click Raise Hand. By phone, dial *9 to raise your hand, then *6 to unmute when called. You get up to three minutes.
To write instead, email districtsecretary@goldengate.org or mail P.O. Box 29000, Presidio Station, San Francisco, CA 94129-9000. Comments are posted weekly with the Board's mail.

meetings.name: Capitol Corridor Joint Powers Authority Board of Directors
meetings.decides: The Capitol Corridor Joint Powers Authority, a partnership of six local transit agencies, manages Capitol Corridor trains between San José, Oakland, Sacramento and Auburn. Its Board sets service, fares and the budget.

usualSchedule.text: Usually five times a year, on the third Wednesday of February, April, June, September and November at 10 am
usualSchedule.note: Meetings switch between the BART Board Room in Oakland and the Solano Transportation Authority in Suisun City. Check the schedule for the place and time.

meetings.watchOnline: You can join by Zoom or by phone, and past meetings are recorded on video. The link and phone number are on the Board of Directors page before each meeting.
howToComment: To write ahead of time, email ccjpaboard@capitolcorridor.org with Public Comment as the subject. Comments sent by 3 pm the day before go to the Board before the meeting.
To speak in person, fill out a Request to Address the Board form at the entrance to the Board Room and hand it to the Secretary before the item comes up. You get two minutes per item.
To speak online or by phone, join the Zoom or call-in number on the agenda, then use Raise Hand, or press *9 on a phone and *6 to unmute when called.

meetings.name: NVTA (Napa Valley Transportation Authority) Board of Directors
meetings.decides: NVTA (Napa Valley Transportation Authority) runs VINE Transit, the Napa Valley bus system, and plans and funds county transportation projects. Its 13 member Board, mostly local elected officials, sets policy and votes on budgets and projects.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the third Wednesday of the month at 1 pm
usualSchedule.note: Some months may be skipped, so check the calendar before you go.

meetings.place: JoAnn Busenbark Board Room, 625 Burnell Street, Napa
meetings.watchOnline: You can join by Zoom or by phone, or watch live on YouTube. The Zoom link is on the Board page and the phone number is on each agenda.
howToComment: Email your comment to info@nvta.ca.gov by 10 am on the meeting day. Put PUBLIC COMMENT in the subject, add the item number if it is about an agenda item, and keep it under 350 words.
To speak in person, go to the meeting. Speak during the general public comment at the start, or when the Chair invites comment on the agenda item.
To speak online, click Raise Your Hand in Zoom when comment is open. By phone, press *9, then press *6 to unmute when called. You get up to 3 minutes.

meetings.name: SolTrans (Solano County Transit) Board of Directors
meetings.decides: SolTrans (Solano County Transit) runs local and Solano Express buses and paratransit service in south Solano County, including Vallejo and Benicia. Its six member Board votes on service, fares, the budget and projects.

usualSchedule.text: Usually the third Thursday of the month at 3:30 pm
usualSchedule.note: Some months have no meeting, so check the calendar and agenda for the date and room.

meetings.place: Vallejo Council Chamber, 555 Santa Clara Street, Vallejo
meetings.watchOnline: You can join by Zoom or by phone. The Zoom link and phone number are on each meeting's agenda, and the meeting page also links to live and archived video.
howToComment: To speak in person, go to the meeting. SolTrans says anyone who wants to address the Board must fill out a Public Comment Request form and agree to its rules.
To speak by Zoom or phone, use the link or number on the agenda. On a phone, press *9 to raise your hand.
You get up to 3 minutes, unless the Board Chair changes the limit.

representatives.name: Find your California state legislators
representatives.description: Type your home address to see your State Senator and your Assemblymember. They vote on state transit funding and on laws that shape how Bay Area agencies work together.

representatives.name: See who sits on MTC
representatives.description: The Metropolitan Transportation Commission (MTC) plans and funds transportation in the nine Bay Area counties. This page lists its commissioners, who are appointed to MTC rather than elected by voters; most are mayors, city council members or county supervisors.

representatives.name: Find your U.S. House member
representatives.description: Enter your ZIP code to find your member of the U.S. House of Representatives. Congress decides federal grants that help pay for large transit projects.

representatives.name: Check whether your city council member sits on the VTA Board
representatives.description: VTA (Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority) says every Board member is an elected official appointed by the city or county they represent: fifteen city council members and three County Supervisors. Twelve vote and six are alternates. The roster shows who they are, so a council office can be an easy door to open.
representatives.linkLabel: See who sits on the VTA Board

email.subject: Please make Bay Area buses and trains work together
email.body:
Dear [Representative's name],

My name is [Your name] and I live in [Your city or neighborhood].

I am writing to ask you to make our buses and trains work together: coordinated schedules, easy transfers, and one fare system.

Please support creating a single regional body with the authority to make that happen.

[Add a sentence or two about a trip that is harder than it should be, such as a missed connection or paying two fares for one journey.]

Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your street address or ZIP code]
tips: Fill in every part in square brackets before you send it.
A sentence about your own trip does more than any statistic.
Include your address or ZIP code so the office knows you live in the district.
Many offices use a contact form on their website. Copy the text and paste it there.

groups.name: Seamless Bay Area
groups.focus: Seamless Bay Area is a nonprofit that works to turn the Bay Area's many transit systems into one connected, easy to use network through advocacy and policy ideas.

groups.name: SPUR
groups.focus: SPUR (San Francisco Bay Area Planning and Urban Research Association) is a member-supported nonprofit in San Francisco, San José and Oakland that researches and promotes better planning, including transportation.

groups.name: Transform
groups.focus: Transform is a nonprofit that works for better transit, safer streets and affordable homes near transit, with campaigns on regional transit funding and Safe Routes to School.

groups.name: Silicon Valley Transit Users
groups.focus: Silicon Valley Transit Users is an independent volunteer group that watches Santa Clara County transit and publishes rider guides, board information and advice.

groups.name: San Francisco Transit Riders
groups.focus: San Francisco Transit Riders is a membership nonprofit that pushes for Muni and other public transit in San Francisco to be fast, reliable and easy to use.

groups.name: Transbay Coalition
groups.focus: Transbay Coalition is a grassroots group, started in 2020, that organizes riders across the nine counties for better transit and safer streets.

groups.name: Public Advocates
groups.focus: Public Advocates is a public interest law and advocacy group whose transit justice work pushes for more transit funding and service for low income riders and riders of color.

groups.name: Friends of Caltrain
groups.focus: Friends of Caltrain is a nonprofit grassroots group that pushes for steady funding and modern service on Caltrain as part of a connected regional transit network.

groups.name: East Bay Transit Riders Union
groups.focus: East Bay Transit Riders Union is a volunteer group of transit riders working to grow and protect public transit in the East Bay, including AC Transit and County Connection buses.

bills.title: Bay Area regional transit sales tax measure
bills.author: Senators Scott Wiener and Jesse Arreguín
bills.explanation: SB 63 created a transit district covering Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo and Santa Clara counties and San Francisco, and let voters decide on a 14 year sales tax to pay for public transit. It also requires an outside review of how efficiently AC Transit, Caltrain, BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) and the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency spend money.
bills.outcomeText: Signed by the governor on October 13, 2025. Voters decided the tax on November 3, 2026; early, unofficial counts posted by the Metropolitan Transportation Commission show it ahead, and each county will certify the final result.
bills.whyItMatters: It put one regional transit sales tax before voters in five counties and requires an outside review of how four large agencies spend money.

bills.title: Emergency state loan to keep Bay Area transit running
bills.author: Assembly Committee on Budget
bills.explanation: AB 117 told the state to lend up to $590 million to the Metropolitan Transportation Commission (MTC), the Bay Area's regional transportation planning agency, by July 1, 2026. MTC can then lend that money to BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit), the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency, Caltrain and AC Transit to keep buses and trains running, and they must pay it back.
bills.outcomeText: Signed by the governor on February 19, 2026, and it took effect right away.
bills.whyItMatters: It lets the regional agency lend up to $590 million of state transit project money to four big agencies to keep buses and trains running, and the loans must be paid back.

bills.title: Faster environmental review for transit projects and route changes
bills.author: Senator Scott Wiener
bills.explanation: SB 71 changes the California Environmental Quality Act, the state's environmental review law, so that more transit projects and transit agency route changes can skip a full review. It also extends an existing exemption for many bus and light rail projects until 2040.
bills.outcomeText: Signed by the governor on October 13, 2025.
bills.whyItMatters: It lets more transit projects and route changes skip a full state environmental review, but it does not address how agencies coordinate schedules or fares.

bills.title: Faster environmental review for big rail station upgrades
bills.author: Senator Dave Cortese
bills.explanation: SB 1375 lets public projects that modernize big train stations skip a full state environmental review if they meet strict rules, such as using clean trains and helping anyone forced to move. Its author has named San José's Diridon Station as an example, but the law itself names no station.
bills.outcomeText: Signed by the governor on September 30, 2026.
bills.whyItMatters: It lets some big train station projects skip a full state environmental review, but it does not address how agencies coordinate schedules or fares.

bills.title: One statewide list of standard transit stop data
bills.author: Assemblymember Patrick Ahrens
bills.explanation: AB 1599 requires the California Department of Transportation to build a statewide list of transit stops by June 1, 2027, with each stop's name, location, ID number and whether it has seats and a shelter. By January 1, 2028, transit agencies must use the same stop names, locations and ID numbers as that list and report which stops have seats and shelters.
bills.outcomeText: Signed by the governor on September 18, 2026.
bills.whyItMatters: It makes transit agencies use the same stop names, locations and ID numbers from one statewide list, so stop data matches across agencies.

bills.title: Letting voters put transit taxes on the ballot by petition
bills.author: Senator Sasha Renée Pérez
bills.explanation: SB 512 would have said in state law that voters can use a petition to put a sales tax for transportation on the ballot in any district that is allowed to have one. The tax could not be higher than the district itself could set, and it would have had to follow the same spending rules.
bills.outcomeText: Vetoed by the governor on October 13, 2025. The Senate did not override the veto, which was recorded as final on March 2, 2026, so the bill did not become law.
bills.whyItMatters: It would have let voters use a petition to put a transportation sales tax on the ballot, a possible new way to fund transit, but it was vetoed.

paragraphs: The 2027 to 2028 session of the California Legislature starts at noon on Monday, December 7, 2026, according to the California Senate's calendar.
New bills can be introduced once the session is open. In the last session the first bills were introduced on its opening day, and bill numbers then appear on the official legislation site.
This page will list new transit bills once they exist. Until then, you can search for bills on the official California legislation site.
